title: Classic Beef Lasagna
subtitle: layers of meaty tomato sauce, creamy ricotta and golden mozzarella — Sunday dinner with lunches all week
imageAlt: A tall slice of beef lasagna with clear layers and a golden cheese top
servingsNote: 8 big squares — dinner for two, twice, plus 4 lunches (freezes well)

breakdown: Onion, garlic, egg, tomato paste & spices

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen beef? Thaw in the fridge overnight (about 24 h).
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). You'll need a 9×13 in (23×33 cm) baking dish.
Put a big pot of salted water on for the noodles while the sauce simmers.
Pick a plain or traditional marinara (no visible basil leaves).
It needs a 20-minute rest after baking so it slices cleanly — plan for it.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep pan over medium-high. Add the beef and onion and cook 8–10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains (71°C / 160°F). Drain off extra fat. Add the garlic for the last minute.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add the marinara, Italian seasoning, salt, pepper and sugar. Simmer gently, partly covered, 15 minutes, stirring now and then. It should be thick, not watery.

steps.title: Boil the noodles
steps.text: Meanwhile cook the noodles in salted boiling water 2 minutes less than the box says (they finish in the oven). Drain, rinse with cool water and lay flat on an oiled sheet so they don't stick.

steps.title: Mix the ricotta
steps.text: Stir the ricotta, egg, ½ cup Parmesan, garlic powder and salt together until smooth.

steps.title: Layer it up
steps.text: Spread 1 cup meat sauce over the bottom of the dish. Then layer: 4 noodles, half the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, ⅓ of the remaining sauce. Repeat: 4 noodles, rest of the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, ⅓ sauce. Finish with 4 noodles, the last of the sauce, 2 cups mozzarella and the Parmesan.

steps.title: Bake covered, then uncovered
steps.text: Cover with foil (tent it or spray the underside so the cheese doesn't stick). Bake at 190°C (375°F) 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 20–25 minutes more until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. The centre should reach 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Rest, then slice
steps.text: Rest 20 minutes before cutting so the layers hold. Cut into 8 squares.

fixIt.fix: The sauce wasn't simmered thick enough or the noodles weren't drained well. Simmer the sauce until a spoon leaves a trail, and always rest 20 minutes before slicing.

fixIt.problem: Top browned before the middle was hot
fixIt.fix: Keep the foil on for the first 25 minutes; if the top darkens early, lay the foil loosely back on.
Rinse with cool water after draining and lay them flat on an oiled sheet.
Season the meat sauce until it tastes good on its own — the noodles and ricotta soak up salt.

saleTip: Ground beef family packs are often $9.99/kg-ish on No Frills flyer weeks, and Classico/No Name marinara goes 2 for $5. Ricotta and mozzarella are cheapest as No Name.
swap: Half ground beef, half mild Italian sausage (casings removed) for extra flavour. Oven-ready noodles also work — skip the boil and add ½ cup water to the sauce.
leftovers: Fridge 4 days. Freeze individual squares wrapped tightly for up to 3 months.
doneness: Ground beef: 71°C (160°F) while browning. Whole lasagna and reheated portions: 74°C (165°F) in the centre.
source: Based on tested classic lasagna methods (Allrecipes 'World's Best Lasagna', Barefoot Contessa): simmered meat sauce, ricotta-egg layer, foil-covered then uncovered bake, 15–20 min rest.
prepAhead: Make the meat sauce up to 3 days ahead.
Assemble the whole lasagna a day ahead, cover and refrigerate; add 10–15 minutes to the covered bake.
Freeze it unbaked for up to 3 months — thaw in the fridge 24–48 h before baking.
reheat: Microwave a square covered, 2–3 minutes at 70% power, until 74°C (165°F). Oven: 180°C (350°F), covered with foil, 20–25 minutes.

basic.note: Meat sauce, noodles and mozzarella — no ricotta layer.

stepNotes.4: Basic: layer sauce, noodles and mozzarella only.

fancy.note: Tall, clean layers with a herb-seasoned ricotta, a mozzarella–Parmesan crust and a slow-simmered sauce.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: simmer the sauce a full 30 minutes for depth.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: stir the Italian seasoning into the ricotta.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: dust each layer with a little Parmesan.

plating: Rest the full 20 minutes — it's what makes tall layers.
Lift squares with a wide spatula onto warm plates.
Spoon a little extra warm sauce beside, not on top.

why.1-0: Ricotta makes the soft, creamy layer. Skip it for a simpler, meatier lasagna.
why.1-1: Egg sets the ricotta so slices stay neat.
why.0-9: A pinch of sugar balances acidic tomatoes.

funFact: The word lasagna likely goes back to the ancient Greek laganon, a flat sheet of dough cut into strips.
